answer: Residual balance slope: each identity starts at zero and its allowed transaction volume grows only with the unspent balance it retains over time. The rule sets a rising marginal cost per identity, since an attacker must park capital that cannot wander into fresh wallets without resetting the slope. Splitting into many identities raises total locked capital by the delta between per-wallet cost and one large pool. An honest operator keeps a shared oasis of liquidity that amortizes the slope across real usage, while a sybil farm pays the full curve on every node.
